title: opum-lore pane: generation-token the refresh guards at session.end, and correct the tick-skip wording (LCLI-707 round-1 minors)
description:
Filed by lore-cli's session from LCLI-707's round-1 review (two MINOR findings), citing LCLI-707 and DEC-172 (4bi).

(a) CROSS-SESSION GUARD LEAK. `session.end` sets `refreshInFlight = false` while a refresh can still be running, and that running refresh's `finally` clears the flag unconditionally — so a slow refresh spanning a `/clear` can clear the SUBSEQUENT session's guard, allowing two refreshes across the boundary (the stacking the guard exists to prevent). Close it with a per-session generation token, so a stale run cannot touch a newer session's guards.

(b) WORDING. "only clock ticks are skipped in flight" (in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md, in CHANGELOG.md's LCLI-705 entry, and in the code comment on the refresh guard) conflates the two guards: the only skip is tick-vs-tick (`tickInFlight`); a tick colliding with an in-flight REFRESH is COALESCED, not skipped. Correct the wording in all three places.

Scope: the refresh/clock guards in hooks/register.tsx and the three wording sites. Not a redesign of the coalescing behaviour LCLI-707 shipped.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The refresh guards are per-session: a refresh still running when session.end fires cannot clear a later session's guard (a per-session generation token, or an equivalent that makes a stale run's cleanup inert).
Proved both ways: a slow refresh spanning session.end plus a new request goes RED without the token and GREEN with it, and both runs are recorded on the task.

The "only clock ticks are skipped in flight" wording is corrected in docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md, in CHANGELOG.md, and in the code comment on the refresh guard: the only skip is tick-vs-tick, and a tick colliding with an in-flight refresh is coalesced.

implementationNotes:
Implemented DEC-172 (4bi)(a) and the wording refinement. `hooks/register.tsx`: the refresh guards carry a session GENERATION — `session.end` bumps `sessionGeneration` and then clears `refreshInFlight`/`refreshQueued`, and a refresh that started under an older generation leaves those flags ALONE in its `finally` (and stops its coalescing loop), so a slow refresh spanning a `/clear` cannot clear the successor session's guard. The wording is corrected in THREE places (the code comment on the refresh guard, docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md, and CHANGELOG.md's LCLI-705 entry): the only thing skipped in flight is a tick meeting a PRIOR tick; a tick meeting an in-flight refresh is coalesced.

Proof both ways (AC2), MEASURED and recorded, not predicted:
- RED without the token: with the `finally` reverted to an unconditional `refreshInFlight = false` (mutation applied and run), the new test "a refresh that outlives session.end cannot clear the successor session's guard (LCLI-709)" FAILS — measured 70 tests / 1 fail, and the failing test is exactly that one.
- GREEN with it: reverted to the committed form, the mod suite is 70 pass / 0 fail (mod typecheck clean).

Also, per the team-lead: a correction note was added to LCLI-708 recording which of its header-map measured-subset counts were MEASURED this round (the two applied mutations, 7/16 and 2/16) and which were carried or reasoned (query-reserve, pack-size, capacity.sources-revert, each 1/16); the header sentence itself is corrected by whichever task next touches that test file.

Gates: `bun run test:mod` 70 pass / 0 fail (mod typecheck clean); `bun test` 5008 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lore check` (exit 0) green.
finalSummary: DEC-172 (4bi)(a): the opum-lore pane's refresh guards are per-session — session.end bumps a generation, so a refresh that started under an older one cannot clear the successor session's guard (proved BOTH ways and measured: RED without the token, the outlived-refresh test fails 70/1; GREEN with it, 70/0). Also corrects the tick-skip wording in three places — the refresh-guard code comment, docs/reference/lore-pane-mod.md and the CHANGELOG — to say the only skip is tick-vs-tick while a tick meeting an in-flight refresh is coalesced. A correction note was added to LCLI-708 recording its MEASURED (7/16, 2/16) vs carried/reasoned (three at 1/16) header counts. Gates: test:mod 70/0, bun test 5008/2/0, lint, typecheck, lore check exit 0. Delivered under opum-control job-0sc8uoe.
